chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah made the sustenance of His Prophets in the crops and the udders, lest they dislike anything from the drops of the sky.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Allah provide sustenance for Prophets through agriculture and animals?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that Allah designated the sustenance of His Prophets through agriculture and animal husbandry to ensure they remained free from aversion to rain, a vital element for both crops and livestock. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on the virtue of agriculture, highlights the Prophets' deep connection to the natural world and their gratitude for divine provision, reinforcing the Shia scholarly view that manual labor and self-sufficiency are noble acts of worship. By linking their livelihood directly to the sky's bounty, the Imam underscores the spiritual purity of Prophets who, despite their high status, relied on tangible, earthly means of sustenance.
